graph.title: LEGO City 7942-1 Off Road Fire Rescue (pickup truck, trailer, pump station)
notes: The manual's pictures are small and several attachment points are inferred. Pieces are mapped to steps by shape, colour and parts-list counts. The totals match the 127-piece inventory exactly, but the exact stud-to-stud partner of some joins (null ports) is approximate.

Minifigure pieces (head, torso, legs, helmet; elements 4194017, 4275338, 9339, 4260036) are not in the parts list, so they are omitted. The airtanks (b107) are shown placed beside the trailer tray with a contact edge. Page 21 shows them worn by the minifigure.

The axe (b127, lego-3835) is held by the minifigure on the cover and is never attached in the steps. To keep the graph in one group, it is linked by a contact edge to the open trailer tray door (b94) as a stowage position. This is an assumption, not a connection the manual shows.

The booklet builds one model: truck, trailer and pump station form a single group. The truck's rear towball-socket plate (b7) hitches to the trailer drawbar ball (b71), and the pump station sits on the trailer top.
The trailer A-frame drawbar with towball is mapped to lego-2508 (b71) because it is the only listed part with a towball. The red clip plate b106 is shown at the drawbar and is joined clip-to-ball.
The sticker sheet (b57) is a single node. Its stickers go on several parts (roof, box doors, side number). One edge to the roof is used.

Sub-assemblies that look alike (the two box+door units, the wheel+tyre pairs) are listed explicitly rather than as repeats, because each copy attaches to a different part and the ids must follow build order.

Tiles and grille tiles (2412b, 2431) have no studs, so their joins are inferred from the pictures. Where the tile sits on a studded plate the join is push-on. The pump station rests on the trailer with contact edges.
